description.narrative: Strengthened multi-sectoral nutrition systems and expanded service delivery led to earlier identification and improved management of malnutrition among children, adolescents and women. Increased access to community screening, counselling and essential nutrition interventions enabled caregivers and households to adopt healthier practices, resulting in more children receiving timely treatment for wasting and more women and adolescents benefiting from preventive services. These integrated efforts contributed to measurable improvements in nutrition status, reduced vulnerability to malnutrition, and progress toward long-term, sustainable outcomes for affected populations. This activity contributed to sublevel results - Prevention of stunting and other forms of malnutrition,Cross sectoral - Social and behaviour change
